extracted.intended_audience: journalists, researchers, and general readers interested in misinformation, fact-checking, and news verification
extracted.subtask_description: A concise organizational profile and history of First Draft News, its mission to combat mis- and disinformation, projects (e.g., CrossCheck), partnerships, and eventual transition of its mission to the Information Futures Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: fight mis- and disinformation online
rubrics_metrics.description: First Draft News was a project 'to fight mis- and disinformation online' founded in 2015 by nine organizations brought together by the Google News Lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization's core stated purpose is combating mis- and disinformation; this underpins its activities (guides, coordination, CrossCheck, partnerships). No explicit scoring guidance on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics in use of eyewitness media
rubrics_metrics.description: Published how-to guides addressing topics such as 'ethics surrounding "use of eyewitness media"'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance implied: provide ethical frameworks and best-practices for how newsrooms and researchers should collect, verify, and use eyewitness-sourced media. The page does not list the specific ethical criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spotting fake footage and hoaxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Published how-to guides on how to 'spot fake footage and hoaxes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance implied: practical verification techniques for identifying manipulated or fabricated audiovisual content; the article does not enumerate the specific methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: CrossCheck: cross-checking between newsrooms to debunk and hinder spread
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms participating in the First Draft's CrossCheck project 'cross-checked' each other, debunked stories, and developed methods to hinder 'the spread of misleading and fabricated content' for the 2017 French, UK, and German elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested practice: collaborative verification (peer cross-checking) among news organizations during high-stakes events (elections) to identify and debunk misinformation, and to develop methods to limit its spread. The page gives the project example but not a step-by-step rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination among newsrooms, fact-checkers, and academia
rubrics_metrics.description: In September 2016, First Draft began coordinating 'efforts between newsrooms, fact-checking organizations, and academic institutions to combat mis- and disinformation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion: multi-stakeholder coordination is a recommended approach to tackle disinformation; the page highlights coordination as a core activity but does not provide detailed standards for how to coordinate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in industry-wide trusted initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: First Draft was a founding member of the Trusted News Initiative and participated in events such as a Trusted News Conference convened by the BBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied best-practice: join and collaborate in cross-industry initiatives (e.g., Trusted News Initiative) and conferences to align practices and responses to systemic disinformation. No scoring or procedural checklist provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and public archiving of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Draft website was archived and 'hosted in perpetuity' by the Internet Archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard: preserve and make verification resources publicly available for long-term access and research. The article notes the archival arrangement but does not provide technical archiving criteria.
